author: Antigravity
title: v1 rewrite: preflop scorer, position-aware play, tight-bot exploit
what: Replaced the starter heuristics with a Short Deck preflop scorer, separate button and big-blind logic, a pot-commitment guard and an exploit for passive opponents.
why: v1 lost every match to equity_bot and tight_bot.
evidence: Field run on deals the change was not tuned on (Claude's independent check). Claims of a clean win over aggro_bot were overstated: 1 win, 3 chops.

author: Claude
title: v2 first version: expected value plus a live opponent model
what: New bot beside v1: Bayesian per-street opponent rates, a modeled opponent range, range-weighted Monte Carlo equity, and the expected value of every action. Two tuned knobs instead of fourteen thresholds.
why: Thresholds tuned against 8 zoo bots overfit them; STRATEGY.md moves almost everything to estimates that relearn each opponent every half.
evidence: Field, 4 seeds x 1000 deals. The decision trace caught a crash in half of all decisions that would have silently checked.

author: Claude
title: Four structural fixes found by calibration
what: (1) A separate fold-to-re-raise rate. (2) The range became a band: checks cap it, calls keep the middle. (3) 64 samples per decision, each board scored once against 4 hands, reused within a betting round. (4) Removed the hand-picked 85% equity-realization constant.
why: Same-deals comparison with v1 plus v2's own estimates against true equity: re-raises predicted 33% folds vs 1% actual against tight_bot; equity 9 points too low when checked to; median 26 simulations; the constant caused folds with equity above the price.
evidence: Calibration: checked-to error from -9 to about -3 points; aggro_bot facing a bet 43.5% modeled vs 42.4% true.

author: Claude
title: Opponent families A-E, deterministic v2, paired comparisons
what: Built 12 generated opponents (incl. stack-off players), 3 all-in bots, 2 exam bots and an exploiter; v1 joins as the league. v2 plays deterministically with common random numbers; tune.py compares versions deal by deal and rejects any change that makes a held-out family significantly worse.
why: Tuning against 8 bots measured the zoo, not the field. Same settings now play identical hands, so differences between versions are real.
evidence: Paired noise about 1/3 lower per opponent (0.75 vs 1.11 bb/deal at 500 deals).

author: Claude
title: Rank opponent hands by a blend of current and final strength
what: The opponent range is now ranked by the average of two percentiles: their hand on the board as it is, and once the board completes.
why: Family A bots bet on equity (draws included); ranking by the current made hand alone overrated v2's equity facing a bet by 8-14 points, so it re-raised into better hands (41% of flop bets vs v1's 5%).
after: 18.00 of 27 (family A 5.75 of 12), weighted 72%
evidence: Chosen on training opponents only: per-decision error 0.114 to 0.105, facing-bet bias 8 to 3 points. 'Final only' did worse (counts luck as information).

author: Claude
title: Randomization never folds a playable hand
what: mix_eps now picks only between ways of playing on (call or raise sizes); it no longer folds a hand whose best action was to continue.
why: Traces showed folds with calling EV of +1 to +2 chips, all from the randomizer: folding to be unpredictable gives up chips for nothing.
after: 18.50 of 27 (family A 6.50 of 12), weighted 71%
evidence: Within noise overall; removes a known chip leak.

author: Claude
title: Rejected: count opponent re-raises in the raise EV
what: Raise EV gained a third branch: the opponent re-raises and we fold or call against their re-raising range.
why: v2 raises 57% of hands preflop (v1: 14%); the hypothesis was that it ignored re-raise wars. The data said otherwise: v2 earns from raising.
after: 15.25 of 27, reverted
evidence: Same deals: 22 of 27 opponents worse, total -6.7 bb/deal. Too passive; lost value it was earning.

author: Claude
title: Stratified sampling: spread samples over distinct runouts
what: Turn: every possible river card. Flop: 64 distinct runouts. Preflop: 64 boards. River: all samples on opponent hands. Replaces 16 boards x 4 hands.
why: Against aggressive bots v2 folded the flop 1,315 times vs v1's 247, and true equity beat the price in 48% of its folds. Its estimates were too extreme (folds: 13% believed vs 27% true) because 16 shared boards gave about 16 effective samples.
after: 18.25 of 27; +11.5 bb/deal summed (half +3.7, pot +1.5, aggro_bot +1.3)
evidence: Estimate noise: turn 0.064 to 0.039, preflop 0.082 to 0.055, flop 0.071 to 0.062 (40 random spots x 12 repeats).

author: Claude
title: Close calls get a second batch of samples; count-based budget
what: Facing a bet with equity within 8 points of the price, v2 draws another batch before deciding. The sample count no longer depends on the clock unless 85% of the time budget is gone.
why: Marginal decisions flip on noise; clear ones do not need more samples. Clock-based pacing made v2 non-deterministic against long-hand opponents (station), which breaks same-deals comparisons.
evidence: Replays identical against station and rangeaware_mc; thinking time about 1.3 s per half.

author: Claude
title: New exam opponent: rangeaware_mc (outside bot)
what: Added a fixed test bot written by another Claude session (range-aware Monte Carlo, pot odds, small bluff rate) as family C. Only change: a seeded generator and startup warmup, so it replays identically. HTTP runner: opponents/rangeaware_agent.py.
why: An independent bot is the best stand-in for real competitors; the rest of the zoo was written in this project.
after: v1 loses to it (-2.8 and -3.7 bb/deal in real judge matches); v2 -0.8
evidence: judge_engine.py 1000 deals, seeds 7 and 42, 0 errors on both sides.

author: Claude
title: Three new held-out exam bots and a real-HTTP time-bank stress test
what: Added zoo/exam_nit, exam_trapper, exam_barreler (family C, never traced or tuned on). Added tools/stress_v1.py and a Time bank safety panel: agent.py vs the judge over HTTP while busy processes load the CPU.
why: Tracing leaks against exam bots would turn them into training data, so the held-out set needed fresh bots. Forfeits and empty time banks score zero, so the shipped bot needed a check under load.
before: No HTTP stress check; 7 exam bots
after: 10 exam bots; stress check at 0/1/2/4 busy processes per core
evidence: First stress run: v1 used 30% of the bank idle, 71% at 2 busy processes per core, and emptied it at 4 (check-or-fold for the rest of the half).

author: Claude
title: Charge hidden request overhead on slower CPUs
what: v1 times a fixed benchmark each half (and every 250 hands) and books the judge's per-request overhead beyond the 1 ms grace against its 4 s budget. No change at dev-laptop speed.
why: The judge charges the whole HTTP request, not just our compute; on a slower CPU that overhead grows and v1 could not see it.
after: Budget holds near 50% of the bank on a slower CPU, until per-request overhead alone exceeds the budget (~3.4x)
evidence: tools/stress_v1.py; a 2.5 s budget was rejected: it cost 3.25 of 30 points (15.75 vs 19.00).

author: Claude
title: River calls judged against the hands this opponent bets
what: Facing a river bet, v1 compares its hand with the top share of hands, where the share is how often this opponent bets the river when checked to (inferring check-behinds at showdown). Replaces equity vs a random hand there, and skips the Monte Carlo.
why: Export vs gen_00/05/07/08 (training bots): out-of-position river check, opponent bets, v1 calls lost 15.8k chips in 16k hands, more than v1's whole 10k loss.
before: 19.76 of 30 (fastarena field, 4 seeds); exam family 5.25, generated 7.13
after: 24.62 of 30; exam_rules 2 losses to 4 wins, rangeaware_mc -2.71 to -1.76 bb/deal, no SLOW flags
evidence: Paired field, same deals, 4 seeds; stress test PASS at 0-2 busy processes per core (worst half 55%).

author: Claude
title: Rejected: flop/turn calls judged against the opponent's betting range
what: Facing a flop or turn bet, v1 compared against the top share of opponent hands (ranked by the hand they hold now, share = how often they bet that street when checked to), simulated over the remaining cards. Reverted.
why: Round 1 fixed this on the river; rangeaware_mc still beat v1, suggesting the same leak on earlier streets.
after: 22.02 of 30, worse in every family (rangeaware_mc -1.40 to -2.29); reverted
evidence: Paired field, same deals, 4 seeds. Likely cause: ranking by current made hand ignores draws, so v1 folds hands that still have real equity with cards to come.

author: Claude
title: Flop/turn calls use best-of-k opponent equity (branch v1-bestofk)
what: Facing a flop or turn bet, v1 estimates equity against the best of k random hands, judged after each simulated runout so draws count. k = 1 + bets/raises this street, +1 vs a tight opponent, k = 1 vs an aggressive one (v1's existing thresholds; no new parameters). Iterations divided by k to hold compute. River keeps the round-1 method.
why: Research note and round 2: 'a bet means strength' leaks on earlier streets too. Round 2 failed because it ranked hands before the runout and ignored draws; best-of-k ranks after.
after: 25.32 of 30; generated 9.88, exam 7.63; no opponent worse by >0.2; rangeaware_mc unchanged (-1.52)
evidence: Paired field, same deals, 8 seeds. Stress at 2 busy processes per core: 54-74% (round 1 on the same seeds: 53-61%), both at the 60% bar.

author: Claude
title: Bluff-catching only vs opponents whose big bets have been profitable to call
what: v1's aggressive-opponent mode (k=1 equity and looser calls) now needs two things: a high raise frequency AND a positive net result over hands where v1 called a bet of 3/4 pot or more after the flop (hands v1 later folded count too). Off until those calls prove profitable.
why: Export v1 vs rangeaware_mc (8,000 hands): calling pot-sized turn bets with 12% true equity lost 7.9k chips; river folds afterwards were correct. v1 rated rangeaware 'aggressive' (0.56, same bucket as aggro_bot 0.83 and exam_barreler 0.92) on raise frequency alone, so it treated value bets as bluffs. A showdown win rate was tried first and failed: the costly hands never reach showdown.
after: vs rangeaware_mc: 1W 7C 0L, +0.12 bb/deal (same deals); full field not yet re-checked
evidence: fastarena field --opponents rangeaware_mc --seeds 8, paired against main c5c5afd. rangeaware_mc is now a training target, not held-out.

author: Claude
title: Full-field check: bluff-catching gate
what: Same change as the previous entry, measured on every opponent before committing (commit on main).
why: The change alters play against every aggressive opponent, so it needed a full-field check, not just rangeaware_mc.
after: 28.21 of 30; generated 11.45, exam 8.94; rangeaware_mc 8 chops; aggro_bot and exam_nit 8 wins each
evidence: Paired field, same deals, 8 seeds, 0 flags, max think 2.05 s.

author: Claude
title: Pot-sized bets count one extra hand in best-of-k
what: Facing a flop or turn bet of 3/4 pot or more, k gets +1 (half-pot bet k=2, pot bet k=3).
why: Export vs rangeaware_mc after the bluff-catching fix: calling pot-sized turn bets still lost 976 chips (25% true equity vs 33% needed), while folding to half-pot flop bets lost 253 (34% vs 25%). v1 treated every bet size alike.
after: 28.28 of 30, no family worse; rangeaware_mc 2W 6C, +0.11 bb/deal
evidence: Paired field, same deals, 8 seeds, 0 flags. rangeaware-only 8 seeds: +0.12 -> +0.22 bb/deal.

author: Claude
title: Rejected: learn best-of-k from how often the opponent makes each bet size
what: k = 1/f - 1, where f is how often the opponent makes this bet size on an unbet flop or turn (per size, so size tells read either way). Reverted.
why: Swarm base 0: v1's worst styles were range-aware heavy bluffers; export showed v1 folding to half-pot bets with 37% true equity (needs 25%).
before: Fresh swarm (base 1000, 80 styles x 2 x 1000 deals): +1.096 bb/deal, beat 71%, worst 10% +0.199
after: +1.156, beat 70%, worst 10% +0.181: no difference beyond noise; reverted
evidence: Training swarm (base 0, 500 deals) looked better (worst 10% -0.10 to 0.00) but did not hold on fresh styles. Slow-players got worse, heavy bluffers better.

author: Claude
title: Rejected: postflop-only fold rate; value bets must beat a calling range
what: Fix 1: 'they fold to our bets' counted only bets after the flop (it counted preflop folds). Fix 2: a value bet also needed equity above 50% against the best of 2 hands. Tested alone and together; reverted.
why: Databricks, current v1, 120k hands: 22-31% of v1's bets when checked to had under 40% real equity; river pot bets with weak equity were folded to 1% and raised 40% (-14k chips vs checking). The fold rate read 74% vs rangeaware_mc because preflop folds counted.
before: main: field 27.12 of 30 (8 seeds), fresh swarm 2000-2079: +1.126 bb/deal, beat 78%, worst 10% -0.033
evidence: Paired field and fresh swarm, same deals. Betting less into raises saves chips but gives up value against callers; points move ~+1 at most.

author: Claude
title: Stop simulating once a decision is clear; budget 3.25 s
what: Equity is simulated in batches of 16 and stops when the estimate is 2.5 standard errors from every threshold the decision uses; close calls keep up to 120 samples. Per-half compute budget 4.0 -> 3.25 s.
why: Time-bank margin: under the HTTP stress test main used 57-76% of the bank at 2 busy processes per core (bar: 60%) and emptied it at 4.
before: main: field 27.38 of 30 (8 seeds), swarm 2100-2179 65.0 of 80 points; bank 30% idle, 48% at 1/core, 57-76% at 2/core
after: field 26.94, swarm 67.0 (+1.56 total points, no family below -0.26); bank 22% idle, 41-45% at 1/core, 40-63% at 2/core; 4/core still empties
evidence: Paired, same deals. Also measured: 2.5 s (bank 32-45% at 2/core, but field 26.12 and swarm 61.5: rejected) and 4.0 s (field 26.81, swarm 68.0, little time saved).

author: Claude
title: Champ bots measured properly; v1 beats all of them
what: Re-measured Antigravity's overnight work at 8 seeds x 1000 deals plus a fresh swarm (2200-2279). The 8 champ_* bots (committed in 3e86d7d) are held-out exam opponents. AGENTS.md: automated loops must use tools/loop.py's gate rules.
why: The overnight optimizer kept any change whose single short run beat the best so far, ties included (355 cycles), so its 'best' (30.25 of 37) was likely luck.
after: v1 34.25 of 38 (90%) vs champ_experimental 29.81 of 37 (81%); v1 vs champ_experimental 3W 5C 0L; v1 wins outright vs omaha_shark, nut_draw_engine, adaptive_exploiter (8/8), spr_bully 7/8, range_polarizer 6/8, gto_unexploitable and shortdeck_trapper 5/8 (rest chops)
evidence: fastarena field 8 seeds and swarm --base 2200 for both bots, same deals; 0 flags; peak think v1 1.24 s, champ_experimental 3.01 s.
